name: What factors indicate that my roof needs to be replaced rather than repaired?

mainEntity.name: What factors indicate that my roof needs to be replaced rather than repaired?

acceptedAnswer.text: Key indicators for roof replacement include widespread shingle damage (missing, cracked, or curled shingles), a roof that is past its expected lifespan (typically 20-25 years for asphalt shingles), significant leaks affecting multiple areas, or a sagging roof deck. While minor leaks or isolated storm damage might be repairable, extensive issues often point to the need for a full replacement to ensure structural integrity and prevent further damage. A professional inspection can help determine the extent of the damage and recommend the most cost-effective solution.
acceptedAnswer.description: Widespread shingle damage, an aging roof, multiple leaks, or a sagging deck often indicate a need for replacement. A professional inspection can clarify the best course of action.
